title: Your Doppelganger Might Share Your DNA 🧬
description:
8 billion people. How many have YOUR face?

• An exact copy is almost impossible: a 2015 study of 8 facial measurements on nearly 4,000 faces put the odds below 1 in a trillion.
• But look-alikes are real: in a 2022 study, 3 face-recognition programs matched 16 of 32 pairs of unrelated look-alikes.
• 9 of those pairs shared many of the same gene variants, and look-alike pairs tended to be similar in height, weight and smoking habits.
• The researchers say that with more people on Earth, look-alikes become more likely.

Sources:
- Joshi et al., Cell Reports (2022): https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111257
- Cell Press / EurekAlert news release (2022): https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/962273
- Sci.News, Look-alike humans have similar DNA: https://www.sci.news/genetics/look-alike-humans-11124.html
- Lucas & Henneberg, Are human faces unique? Forensic Science International (2015): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26441304/
- ScienceAlert, the chances of you having a doppelgänger: https://www.sciencealert.com/here-s-the-chances-of-you-having-a-doppelgaenger
- Christian Science Monitor, How likely are you to meet your exact doppelgänger? (2016): https://csmonitor.com/Science/2016/0717/How-likely-are-you-to-meet-your-exact-doppelgaenger

notes: All faces are generic busts generated from random parameters (no likeness, no photos). Facts: Lucas & Henneberg 2015 (Univ. of Adelaide, Forensic Sci Int): 8 facial measurements on ~4,000 faces from the US Army ANSUR database; chance that someone matches you on all 8 is below 1 in a trillion (ScienceAlert, CSMonitor). Joshi, Esteller et al. 2022 (Cell Reports 40(8):111257): 32 look-alike pairs photographed by artist Francois Brunelle; 3 facial recognition algorithms; 16 pairs grouped by all three; 9 of those 16 clustered genetically on 19,277 common SNPs; weight, height, smoking and education correlated within pairs (EurekAlert release, Sci.News). Esteller: with a population of 7.9 billion, look-alike repetitions are increasingly likely. Caveats kept in script: 'tended to share' (correlation, small sample, mostly European). The 'eight billion' is the world population (~8.2 billion in 2025-26). Height chart and scales are illustrative, no specific values claimed. Cigarettes shown as plain objects only.
